_comment: Tier-2: verifies febio::linear_elasticity#7 — a hex8 with a repeated node id in its connectivity (the classic off-by-one in a generated mesh) is NOT rejected. The run reaches N O R M A L T E R M I N A T I O N with exit 0 and only emits a WARNING box '1 isolated vertex removed.', but the stress is materially wrong. The fixture runs the same one-element uniaxial deck with correct and degenerate connectivity and asserts: both terminate normally (the failure really is silent), the correct run is x/y symmetric while the degenerate one is not, and the two stress states differ by more than 10% relative. Verified 2026-08-03 on FEBio 4.12.0.86045466d: correct sx=sy=1.64474220205, sz=11.2026953216; degenerate sx=2.05167782746, sy=1.48697290222, sz=11.2776298464. Fails in BOTH directions — if FEBio starts rejecting degenerate elements, or if the wrong answer silently becomes right. Skips cleanly when no febio4 binary is installed.
